title: Presenting a Mountain Dining Plans Card at a Collective Outlet
content:
A card on a plan in the Mountain Dining Plans range is presented at the till and the bill, after the plan's card reduction, is taken off the balance. The card is presented only while the plan record stands in the active state, and that state is taken from the collective's own record of the plan as it stands before the card is taken.

The outlet must be one the plan covers and must stand at a mountain the plan is valid at; a card presented elsewhere is refused at the till and the guest pays by other means. On the plan's blackout dates the card is not taken at table service outlets, though quick service outlets take it as usual. Alcohol and resort retail are paid for on the card only where the plan allows them. A transaction above the plan's per-transaction cap, or one that would take the day past the plan's daily cap, is refused rather than split. Where the bill is larger than the balance, the balance is taken and the rest is paid by other means; the balance never goes below nothing. A plan whose balance runs to nothing with no automatic top-up set is marked empty — it stands in the exhausted state — until a fresh load clears.

## What is taken off the balance

The figure taken off the balance is the bill less the plan's card reduction, and it is that reduced figure, not the bill as presented, that the balance answers for.

## What the till is deciding

| What is presented | What decides it | What follows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the card at an outlet of a kind the plan does not cover | the kinds of outlet the plan covers | refused at the till, and the guest pays by other means |
| the card at an outlet standing at a mountain the plan is not valid at | the mountains the plan is valid at | refused at the till, and the guest pays by other means |
| the card at a table service outlet on one of the plan's blackout dates | the plan's blackout dates | not taken at that outlet on that date, while quick service outlets take it as usual |
| alcohol, on a plan that does not admit it | what the plan admits | not paid for on the card |
| resort retail, on a plan that does not admit it | what the plan admits | not paid for on the card |
| a transaction above the plan's per-transaction cap | that cap | refused, and not split into smaller transactions |
| a transaction that would take the day past the plan's daily cap | that cap | refused, and not split into smaller transactions |
| the card while the plan stands in any state other than active | the state on the plan record | the card is not presented |

## A bill larger than the balance, on hypothetical figures

A bill of $60.00 is presented at an outlet the plan covers, at a mountain the plan is valid at, on a plan whose card reduction is 10 per cent and whose balance stands at $40.00. The figure the balance answers for is the bill less the reduction, which is $54.00. The balance holds $40.00, so $40.00 is taken and the remaining $14.00 is paid by other means. The balance stands at nothing and does not go below it.

Where no automatic top-up is set on that plan, the plan is marked empty from that point and stands in the exhausted state until a fresh load clears.
